column1: # The published errata of the Revised Haskell 98 Report: all 18 entries, in their order, of
# https://www.haskell.org/definition/haskell98-revised-bugs.html, the last dated September 2008. rhc's text is the
# Report of December 2002 plus these errata (the haskell98 roadmap's D38). The online Report, and so pristine/, has
# none of them applied. An erratum that changes the Report's code is applied in the modules of this directory and is
# an entry of overlay.tsv; every other one is about prose, the grammar or an index, and the column `where` says what
# Columns: id; date; section (the Report's, or the index); erratum, in short; kind (code, prose, grammar, index);
# online (unapplied: the old wording is in the online text and the new is not; untested; book: the printed book only);
# here (applied in these files, or none); where; reading (R1 to R54 of docs/plans/language/haskell98.md, the
# haskell98 roadmap, and of its drafts' results/E9/readings.md; - for none).

column4: The production of an end-of-line comment admits --: although it is a varsym: comment -> dashes [ any<symbol | :> {any} ] newline
Labelled fields are matched in the order they are named in the pattern's field list, not in the order of the declaration
column8: rhc's translation of patterns, and a test of the order of evaluation

column4: Matching a constructor pattern using labeled fields, not "matching against a constructor": a wording
n+k: the x of "succeeds if x >= k" should be v
Table 4.1 lacks =<<, infixr 1; the HTML captions the table "Table 2"
column8: nothing to do: Prelude.hs declares infixr 1 =<<

column4: The enumFrom family on Float and Double is strict in all its arguments, and the code's enumFrom and enumFromThen are not: a seq is added to the instances for Float and Double
column8: Prelude.hs, instance Enum Float and instance Enum Double: enumFrom, enumFromThen (overlay ov.prelude.enumfloat)

column4: properFraction x is (n,f) with x = n+f, n integral, |f| < 1, n zero or of x's sign, and f zero or of x's sign: the old wording fails at zero
The example of do notation shows its prompt late, being buffered: use putStrLn, or set stdout unbuffered first
lex: an identifier may start with an underscore: isIdInit c = isAlpha c || c == '_' in the third guard, and '_' out of isSingle
In the third production of export, the qvar in parentheses after qtycls is var, as in 5.2
approxRational returns the simplest rational within the closed interval, not the open one
column8: nothing to do in the code, which the erratum describes; a test pins the closed interval

column4: The law map index (range (l,u)) = [0..rangeSize (l,u)] is bogus: map (index (l,u)) (range (l,u)) = [0 .. rangeSize (l,u) - 1]
column8: a test of the corrected law

column4: genericTake, genericDrop and genericSplitAt treat a negative number as 0, as take, drop and splitAt do, instead of calling error: their code is replaced
column8: List.hs, genericTake, genericDrop, genericSplitAt, now the erratum's code (overlay ov.list.generic)
